source.title: Carboxymethyl Chitosan and Gelatin Hydrogel Scaffolds Incorporated with Conductive PEDOT Nanoparticles for Improved Neural Stem Cell Proliferation and Neuronal Differentiation

formulation.evidence: CMCS solution (2%, w/v) and Gel solution (2%, w/v) were firstly mixed with a ratio of 2:1 (v/v).
CMCS solution (2%, w/v) and Gel solution (2%, w/v) were firstly mixed with a ratio of 2:1 (v/v).
the hydrogels were cross-linked in an ethanol/MES buffer (80%, v/v, pH 6.0) containing 50 mM of EDC and NHS.

processing.evidence: The frozen samples were further lyophilized for 48 h in a freeze-dryer
After incubation at room temperature (RT) for 24 h, the hydrogels were rinsed overnight

conductivity.evidence: the conductivity of CMCS/Gel hydrogel is about (3.14 ± 0.36) × 10−6 S·cm−1

swelling_ratio.evidence: the CMCS/Gel hydrogel showed the highest swelling rate, which increased dramatically to (2900 ± 460)% in the first 24 h

degradation_time.evidence: The CMCS/Gel hydrogel lost approximately (45.27 ± 2.21)% in weight at week 6

biology.cell_type: neural stem cells from fetal Sprague Dawley rat hippocampus

culture_days.evidence: although the cell viability of all samples decreased to some extent after 14 days

notes: Porosity (95.62%) reported but no field. Conductivity attributed to ionic conductivity. Compressive modulus only in figure. Degradation in PBS with 2 mg/mL lysozyme at 37 °C.
